newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson wins AXE deal with Interoute.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson wins AXE deal with Interoute.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications group AB LM Ericsson said on Thursday it won an order for AXE TransLocal switching equipment from telephone operator Interoute Telecommunications PLC.

Ericsson said the order will make Interoute the first telecoms operator to use a combination of Ericsson Access Node Switches (ANS) and AXE TransLocal switches to offer advanced services transparently and cost-effectively across Europe.
The AXE TransLocal switch, to be installed in London, will be a central part of Interoute's European network which is based on Ericsson ANS, Ericsson said in a statement.
It said its ANS can be used by new operators, both as an entry level switchor as a Virtual Private Networks access switch.
"As the end-user and network demands increase the Ericsson ANS switch can be converted via easy software changes to a complementary access solution for AXE switches," the statement said.

Ericsson said the AXE TransLocal switch was three switches in one with all the subscriber access functions and services of an AXE local switch, plus the interconnection and signalling functions of AXE transit and international gateway switches.
Interoute Telecommunications is a British based international telecommunications operator that is positioning itself for liberalisation of the European telecommunications market.
